what: 3M makes industrial and consumer products built on its materials science: adhesives and tapes, abrasives, films for screens and vehicles, respirators and personal safety gear, and Post-it and Scotch consumer brands.
customers: Manufacturers, carmakers, electronics firms, construction and safety buyers, and consumers through retailers.
money: abrasives, tapes, adhesives, respirators and industrial films
films and materials for vehicles, displays and electronics
Post-it, Scotch, Command and Filtrete products
moat: Tens of thousands of patents and a research tradition that lets it sell small, specified components at good margins across many industries.
risks: Legal settlements over earplugs and PFAS chemicals require payments over many years
Revenue has barely grown, about 2% in the last financial year
Industrial demand follows the manufacturing cycle
Spinning off the healthcare business removed a steadier segment
opportunities: Margins have improved under new management through cost cuts and portfolio pruning
Litigation liabilities are now largely settled with defined payment schedules
Operating margins near 19% leave room for improvement toward peer levels
watch: Organic sales growth, which has been the weak point, and free cash flow after legal payments.
